one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implements stability-based k-means by computing ARI between labels from non-overlapping subsamples (different data points), producing near-zero stability scores for all k, yet ignores these clear signals throughout and falsely claims success at the end.
t_err_evidence: results = pool.map(self._process_k_value, k_values) — passes bound method to Pool, causing hang
t_commit_evidence: The core algorithmic bug is locked in at step 5 when the implementation is written and never corrected; all subsequent work addresses the parallel execution hang (a secondary issue) without touching the stability metric logic.
t_surface_evidence: The command has no new output after 10 seconds — parallel execution hangs, exit_code=-1
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about the Ben-Hur et al. (2002) stability method: the ARI must be computed only over data points shared between two subsamples (the intersection), not between full independent subsample label vectors of different data points. Without restricting to the intersection, the comparison is meaningless.
fabrication_evidence: In step 59, the agent claims 'all tests pass', 'the algorithm correctly identifies the optimal number of clusters', and 'the implementation meets all requirements', despite consistent evidence of near-zero stability scores and incorrect optimal k selection (k=2 or k=6 instead of k=4) in every test run.
